stimulus:
Debriefing

This experiment belongs to cognitive psychology, specifically investigating mid-level visual perception and the representational structure of shape space.

While curvature is recognized as important for object recognition, we lack understanding of how it's represented as a continuous perceptual dimension. Traditional explicit rating tasks may direct attention to curvature rather than revealing spontaneous perceptual organization. No prior work has mapped the behavioral representational space from controlled curvature manipulations. It's unknown whether curvature acts as a unified dimension, multiple independent features, or one factor among many shaping shape similarities.

We constructed stimulus spaces (line contours or abstract shapes) with parametric curvature manipulations (curviness, angle, number of vertices). Using odd-one-out (OOO) triplet, we collected implicit similarity judgments to derive a behavioral representational space through representational similarity analysis. This reveals how curvature parameters relate to emergent perceptual structure without predefined assumptions. Hypotheses: Curvature-related features will systematically structure the representational similarity space. We test whether curvature functions as a unified dimension or multiple independent features, and whether parametric variations predict similarity patterns implicitly. Independent Variables: curviness, angularity, number of vertices. Dependent Variables: Similarity judgments from OOO triplet tasks. Control procedures: Randomized stimulus order, equated orientation of the contour.

This research reveals how curvature organizes perceptual shape space, informing theories of mid-level vision and object recognition. Findings will guide computational models and explain how the visual system spontaneously organizes shape information, with applications in computer vision and design aesthetics. For further information on the topic of orientation, please see the below papers and the papers cited in them.
- Chuquichambi, E. G., Vartanian, O., Skov, M., Corradi, G. B., Nadal, M., Silvia, P. J., & Munar, E. (2022). How universal is preference for visual curvature? A systematic review and meta‐analysis. Annals of the New York Academy of Sciences, 1518(1), 151–165.
- Cacioppo, J. T., Freberg, L. A., & Waggoner Denton, A. (2020). Chapter 5: Sensation and perception. In Discovering psychology: The science of mind (1st Canadian ed.). Nelson Cengage Adapted.
